children: 2019 ET - The Nikkei Stock Average rises 1.0% to 65085.40 in early trade, tracking Wall Street's gains overnight. Concerns over the impact of high interest rates on the AI boom may ease, given Thursday's fall in U.S. Treasury yields. "Yields continued to retrace from their cycle highs despite the hot U.S. inflation report, thanks to dovish Fed comments which have cooled bets of an October rate hike," says Matt Simpson, senior market analyst at StoneX, in a commentary. Among the best performers on Japan's benchmark index, Nomura Research Institute rises 5.7%, Sanrio advances 5.2%, and Konami Group adds 5.0%. The dollar is at 158.16 yen versus Y157.92 around Thursday's Tokyo market close. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

1943 ET - Japanese stocks may rise, tracking Wall Street's gains overnight. Concerns over the impact of high interest rates on the AI boom may ease, given Thursday's fall in U.S. Treasury yields. Investors are likely to focus on Fed Chair Warsh's fireside chat at an IMF event in Bangkok today for any clues on the central bank's rate-increase trajectory. Nikkei futures opened 730 points higher at 65405 on the SGX. The dollar is at 158.11 yen versus Y157.92 around Thursday's Tokyo market close. The Nikkei Stock Average closed 4.9% lower at 64425.95 on Thursday. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

1813 ET - Alcoa CFO Molly Beerman says the company thinks that the momentum displayed in the recent quarter will to continue through the end of the year. "We are expecting higher production and shipments in both (the aluminum and alumina) segments as the improved refining system stability is maintained and the smelting portfolio continues to deliver productivity through incremental output and cost discipline," Beerman says on a call with analysts. "While we expect some higher direct input costs from elevated market prices and planned maintenance to support continued operational stability, the underlying performance remains very strong headed into the final quarter of the year." (connor.hart@wsj.com)

1801 ET - Alcoa CEO Bill Oplinger opens the company's third-quarter earnings call by addressing the fatality that occurred at its Alumar smelter in Brazil last month. "There is no production target, financial result or business objective that is more important than ensuring every employee and contractor returns home safely every day," Oplinger says. Moving forward, Oplinger says Alcoa is committed to ensuring it learns from the event and takes necessary actions to strengthen the company's safety culture, reduce risks across its operations and hold itself accountable to the highest safety standards. (connor.hart@wsj.com)

1748 ET - Shopify appears to be testing higher prices on select annual plans, Jefferies analysts say in a research note. The firm's research team recently noticed different prices for Shopify's annually billed Grow and Advanced plans when visiting from different devices, with the company's Grow plan increasing 13% to $89 a month and its Advanced plan rising 20% to $359 a month, the analysts say. "The change appears to be a targeted A/B test: We see no change to Basic pricing, monthly Grow or Advanced plans, or Shopify Plus plans," they write. Overall, the analysts see the increases as a positive signal that long-awaited price increases are actually in the works. However, if the hikes are limited to the select increases that the analysts found today, investors are likely to be underwhelmed by the breadth and magnitude, they add. (connor.hart@wsj.com)

1553 ET - Treasury yields eased as investors seem to seek safe fixed-income positions. Fresh U.S. indicators show the economy still resilient and inflation running high. Just a week ago, such combination would have sent yields rising, but the mood has changed. Investors now seem more concerned about the effect of high interest rates on AI growth expectations. September industrial production tomorrow is forecast to accelerate, according to a WSJ consensus. Fed Chairman Warsh's speech at an IMF event in Bangkok tonight is likely to set expectations for interest rates. The 10-year yield fell 0.102 percentage point, to 5.086%. The two-year fell 0.053 point, to 4.747%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

1502 ET - U.S. natural gas futures end the session mixed with the front-month gaining while subsequent months lose ground. The EIA reported a 67 Bcf storage injection for last week, which was below the five-year average and smaller than the 75 Bcf estimate of analysts in a WSJ survey. "Following a brief cooler period over the upcoming weekend, temperatures are expected to remain above normal for the eastern half of the U.S. for the rest of October," Blake Owen of Pinebrook Energy Advisors says in a note. "These moderate fall temperatures should lead to lower power demand while also limiting any early season heating demand, creating conditions for fairly robust storage injections over the next three to four weeks." Natural gas for November delivery settles up 1.2% at $3.236/mmBtu.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

1443 ET - Gold futures snap a three-session losing streak with support from a drop in U.S. yields and a weaker dollar. "While the immediate pressure has eased, I would be reluctant to interpret today's gains as a clear signal that the correction is over," Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com says in a note. Central bank purchases of the metal cushion the downside, but with this week's higher-than-expected U.S. inflation readings, "the Fed will have to hike again and maintain a hawkish bias for a while, especially if oil prices continue to push higher from here on," he adds. Front month gold rises 1.5% to $4,147.70 a troy ounce. Front-month silver gains 2.3% to $56.837 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

1320 ET - September saw the slowest pace of rent decline in three years, Realtor.com says. Today's rental market is being shaped by the cooling of the supply wave in the Sun Belt, renters moving to more affordable alternatives, and AI-driven job growth in the Bay Area. The median asking rent for studio, one- and two-bedroom properties across the 50 largest U.S. metros fell 0.4% year over year to $1,694. This marks the 38th consecutive month of annual declines. Nearly 43.9% of rental listings across the 50 largest metros offered a concession in September, up 1.3 percentage points from a year earlier. The strongest rent growth is in the Bay Area. Median asking rent in San Jose rose 6% to a new high of $3,565, while San Francisco rent increased 4.8% to $3,057. (chris.wack@wsj.com)

1116 ET - Bombardier's fundamentals are strong and a recent pullback has brought the stock to an attractive level, according to Cameron Doerksen of National Bank of Canada. The analyst says that the company has a healthy backlog of $21.8 billion, with new jet order activity still robust going into 3Q. The jet maker is expected to show "solid aftermarket growth while the Defense segment backdrop remains highly positive." Doerksen raises the stock's rating to outperform from sector perform, but lowers the price target to C$360 from C$379. Shares are trading 4% higher at C$301.50, and are up 29% year-to-date.(adriano.marchese@wsj.com)

1100 ET - The northeastern Spanish region of Catalonia is expected to grow faster than Madrid for the first time in six years, BBVA economists say. The bank expects Catalonia's economy to expand 2.3% in 2027, boosted especially by improved goods exports, while Madrid region is expected to grow 2.1%. Catalonia, with its bigger population and industrial base, historically had a larger economy than Madrid, but its GDP was overtaken by the capital's in 2017. The two regions account for the highest share of the Spanish economy, and both will continue to benefit from services exports, including tourism. BBVA expects Spanish GDP growth to slow to 2.1% next year, from 2.6% in 2026, as high energy prices, inflation and elevated interest rates damp activity. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)

1047 ET - The Bank of Japan is likely to raise interest rates again before year-end, providing more support to the Japanese yen, MUFG Bank's Lee Hardman says in a note. BOJ board member Junko Koeda said Thursday the central bank shouldn't become overly cautious about raising rates given upside risks to inflation. Her comments boosted the yen along with broad-based risk aversion encouraging investors to seek safe-haven assets, Hardman says. MUFG expects the BOJ to leave rates steady on October 30 but increase rates in December, lifting the yen. The dollar falls 0.2% to 158.04 yen, having reached a one-week low of 157.57 overnight, according to LSEG. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
